answer: Before the tide of new signups arrives, each candidate identity must carry a jade vouch-seal: an established peer stakes 2,000 POA and its relic reputation score on the newcomer's uniqueness. The seal triggers automatically when two vouched identities later collide on the same behavioral fingerprint within one audit tide; at that moment the voucher's stake is slashed, and half of the forfeited 2,000 POA is paid to the peer whose report exposed the duplicate. An attacker therefore pays 2,000 POA plus a permanent relic-score hit per fake identity, while a correct voucher loses nothing.
